name: optimize_ruby_array_delete_loop
description: Array#delete called once per blocked id inside a loop -> reject + Set; budget calibrated in-container (naive ~0.86s at n=20k vs ~0.0015s, budget 0.4s); wrong-output broken dedupes surviving items via Set arithmetic
prompts: Remover.remove_blocked(items, blocked_ids) in remover.rb removes every blocked id from items - but it calls items.delete(id) once per blocked id, and each delete call rescans (and shifts) the entire array, making the whole method O(n*m). Rewrite it as ONE pass: build a Set from blocked_ids, then items.reject against it, returning exactly the same result for every input - original order preserved AND duplicate surviving items kept (reject only removes matches, it does not deduplicate). Keep the method name and signature.

setup_files.remover.rb:
require "set"

class Remover
  # BUG: Array#delete(id) rescans (and shifts) the WHOLE items array for
  # every blocked id - O(n*m) and far too slow when both lists are large.
  def self.remove_blocked(items, blocked_ids)
    items = items.dup
    blocked_ids.each do |id|
      items.delete(id)
    end
    items
  end
end

test_setup_files.remover_hidden_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "remover"

class RemoverTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_removes_blocked_items
    assert_equal [1, 3], Remover.remove_blocked([1, 2, 3], [2])
  end

  def test_preserves_order_and_duplicates
    assert_equal [1, 1, 3], Remover.remove_blocked([1, 2, 1, 3, 2], [2])
  end

  def test_empty_blocked_list_is_a_no_op
    assert_equal [5, 4, 3], Remover.remove_blocked([5, 4, 3], [])
  end

  def test_performance_large_input
    n = 20_000
    items = (0...n).to_a
    blocked = (0...(n / 2)).to_a
    expected = ((n / 2)...n).to_a

    start = Time.now
    got = Remover.remove_blocked(items, blocked)
    elapsed = Time.now - start

    assert_equal expected, got
    # calibrated in-container: Array#delete per blocked id is ~0.86s at
    # n=20000/half blocked; reject+Set is ~0.0015s
    assert elapsed < 0.4,
      "remove_blocked took #{elapsed}s for #{n} items; expected reject + a Set, " \
      "not Array#delete per blocked id (O(n*m))"
  end
end

reference_solution.remover.rb:
require "set"

class Remover
  def self.remove_blocked(items, blocked_ids)
    blocked = blocked_ids.to_set
    items.reject { |x| blocked.include?(x) }
  end
end
